situation (example wording): Any single-figure answer: "murders in Dallas in 2024", "violent crime rate in Chicago 2024", "violent crime rate for the US in 2025", "Houston clearance rate for murder in 2022", "how is domestic violence defined?"
what the app does today: A place-and-crime label as the first line ("Dallas, Texas: murders, 2024."), then the figure on the next line.
proposed behavior: A text-only answer opens with one sentence. A table or chart answer opens with a Title Case title, then sentence notes, then the Source line. A one-row, several-column answer opens with its sentence and keeps the one-row table. A clearance rate is a sentence. A city is named by its short name in the possessive ("Chicago's violent crime rate in 2024 was 539.8 per 100,000."), with the state only when two places of that name both have 100,000 people or more (P28) ("Kansas City, Missouri's"); a state is "Colorado's", and a name ending in s takes 's ("Texas's"). The nation reads "The United States had a violent crime rate of 327.6 per 100,000 in 2025." Say "data", not "reports". The ranking and coverage titles, the county-wide and "getting better" decline sentences, "murders" for Crime Index counts and "murder victims" for NIBRS victims are unchanged. The definitions answer is only text: its sentence and the Source line, with no title.
exact default or choices offered: The sentence for a text-only answer; the Title Case title with sentence notes for a table or chart.
why: Jeff 2026-11-18 (through the coordinator): answer headlines as sentences, titles for tables and charts.
